actual_read.finding: json.Unmarshal precedes the HTTP status check; a non-JSON 401 or 403 therefore returns MALFORMED_REPLY/exit1. A decoded non-2xx response returns exit3 even for 503. This function cannot supply the required doctor classification unchanged.

amendment: The original requirement to use v2CallContext is replaced with reuse of v2EnvelopeFor, the existing credential/context construction and frozen request/reply protocol constraints. Doctor may implement its own bounded no-redirect transport entirely within cli_doctor.go. cli_v2.go and all other callers remain outside writable scope.
conditions: Validate a loopback HTTP(S) URL without userinfo/query/fragment before credentials or network use. Use a fresh host-level context with empty cliConfig and no session/project/writer arguments; no initialization, renewal or persistent mutation.
Use the existing typed envelope builder for host.status with an empty payload, actual command/client IDs and current protocol. Preserve bearer handling without printing credentials.

Never follow redirects. Bound request duration and response size. Classify HTTP401/403 as authorization blocked/exit3 independently of whether the body is JSON. Classify HTTP503/other5xx as failed check/exit1; body parsing cannot convert these into success or auth refusal.

For 2xx replies, validate the full frozen CommandResponse and HostStatusResult, exact protocol_version/command_id/method/client_id, and require COMPLETED. Missing, wrong or malformed identities and ACKNOWLEDGED/IN_PROGRESS cannot complete doctor. Structured REJECTED responses retain the reviewed authorization/resource versus protocol/check distinction.

Retain health DOWN/HTTP503 exit1 and discovery NOT_FOUND exit3. No arbitrary body/error text or credential values may reach output. Health UP and empty host inventories retain NOT_REPORTED_BY_HOST and provider NOT_CHECKED semantics.

Add focused non-JSON401, non-JSON403 and non-JSON503 controls within cli_doctor_test.go, plus malformed2xx, identity, redirect and secret controls already required. All original cli_contract exit assertions remain byte-identical; only its positive host.status handler is writable.
